title: Manna Drive Thru
subject: Criminal Law & Procedure
stem:
During a Bible-study break, Martha drove through the pickup lane of Manna Drive-Thru, a privately owned coffee stand near a Bible college. When she reached the order speaker, she said to John, the cashier, “There is a man across the street with a rifle. He can see the register. If you do not do exactly what I tell you, he will shoot you. Put all the money from the register into a bag and hand it to me when I drive up.”

John could not see anyone across the street and was unsure whether anyone was there. Unwilling to risk being shot, he put $500 from the register into a paper bag and handed it to Martha at the pickup window. Martha drove away but was arrested shortly afterward. She had lied about the man with the rifle and had acted alone.

Of what crime or crimes can Martha be convicted?
call: Of what crime or crimes can Martha be convicted?
rightExplanation:
D is correct. Martha’s threat of immediate shooting pressure made the taking robbery-level, even though the armed person was imaginary. The cashier gave the cash because he feared immediate harm. That keeps the case in the force/threat lane, not the consent-title lane.

Gold Key: Robbery is aggravated larceny. Larceny is lesser-included in robbery. For one taking, the defendant may be convicted of robbery or the lesser larceny, but not both as separate convictions.

Silver Key: When the finalists are “robbery and larceny” versus “robbery or larceny,” the test is not asking whether both sets of elements are present. It is asking whether the convictions can stack for one taking.

c3.label: CUT A — Embezzlement
c3.text: Wrong theft frame. The stem shows a cashier surrendering money under immediate threat, not property entrusted to the defendant. This is anchor-assisted.

c3.label: CUT B — False pretenses
c3.text: Wrong neighboring theft frame. The lie matters, but the operative pressure is fear of immediate harm. This is anchor-assisted.

c3.label: CLASH C vs. D
c3.text: Both are built around robbery + larceny. The axis is conviction stacking for one taking.

c3.label: CALL D
c3.text: Apply the Gold Key: larceny is lesser-included in robbery. One taking supports robbery or lesser larceny, not both convictions.

studentScript: Threat lane. The cashier surrendered money because he feared immediate harm. Cut embezzlement and false pretenses as wrong theft frames. C and D fight on and versus or. The call asks convictions from one taking. Gold Key: robbery contains larceny. Do not stack. Pick D.

A.signal: The stem is a threat-at-the-window taking, not a prior entrusted-possession scenario.
A.lawyer: Embezzlement requires property entrusted to or lawfully possessed by the defendant before conversion.

B.signal: The lie is visible, but the cashier handed over cash because of immediate fear.
B.lawyer: False pretenses requires obtaining title through misrepresentation; here the operative taking is by threat.

C.signal: The word 'and' is the trap; the call asks convictions, not elements present.
C.lawyer: Larceny is lesser-included in robbery; both cannot be separate convictions for the same taking.

D.lawyer: Threat-based taking supports robbery; larceny remains lesser-included.

goldKeys.statement: The theft frame follows how possession/title moved: embezzlement needs entrusted possession; false pretenses needs title by fraud; robbery needs force or threat.
goldKeys.trigger: A theft question with embezzlement, false pretenses, larceny, and robbery in the answer set.

goldKeys.statement: Robbery is aggravated larceny; for one taking, larceny is lesser-included, so the conviction answer is robbery or larceny, not both.
goldKeys.trigger: Answer choices contrast 'robbery and larceny' with 'robbery or larceny.'

silverKeys.statement: When the finalists are 'X and Y' versus 'X or Y,' the question is usually about stacking, not whether both labels seem factually present.
silverKeys.trigger: And/or answer pair with greater and lesser theft offenses.

silverKeys.statement: Lock the call word 'convicted.' A facts-present answer can still be wrong if the convictions merge.
silverKeys.trigger: Call asks 'crime or crimes can be convicted' instead of 'what elements are present.'

remediation.title: Theft frames + one-taking merger
remediation.signal: Robbery, larceny, false pretenses, and embezzlement appear together.
remediation.studentMove: First choose the theft frame by how the property moved; then check if the call asks convictions.
remediation.tinyRule: Force/threat beats title-by-fraud; robbery contains larceny.
remediation.trap: Picking both robbery and larceny because both sets of elements seem present.
